content.text: I just got the April exam week schedule and my daughters' school events for mid-month. There are some overlapping commitments and I need to sort out the calculator order for the competition team before their April 15 training. Can you help me work through this and figure out what I need to do?
I'll dig into your recent activity and current calendar/email/tasks to piece this together. Let me start by reading the relevant context.

tasks.title: Compile individual performance summaries for all 35 Class 10A students
tasks.description: Create detailed performance summary for each student covering: current grades, participation level, strengths/weaknesses, recommendations. Need to have ready for parent-teacher conference on March 15.

tasks.title: Prepare math competition presentation materials for parents
tasks.description: Create presentation slides explaining: competition details, training schedule, time commitment, selection criteria, benefits for students. Parents need clear information to make informed decisions about student participation.

tasks.title: Follow up with Li Ming's parents about behavioral concerns
tasks.description: Schedule individual meeting with Li Fang (parent) to discuss Li Ming's classroom behavior issues. Need to present specific examples and proposed solutions. Parent requested separate meeting after main conference.

tasks.title: Update class WeChat group with semester exam schedule
tasks.description: Post final exam schedule for all subjects to class parent WeChat group. Include dates, times, and preparation recommendations.

tasks.title: Finalize March duty swap arrangement with Zhang Hui
tasks.description: Confirm duty swap details with Teacher Zhang Hui for March 12 afternoon homeroom supervision. Submit formal request to Vice Principal Zhou by March 5 (5 working days before March 12). Follow up on approval status.

tasks.title: Coordinate with husband for March 19 daughters' pickup
tasks.description: Husband confirmed availability for March 19 afternoon (2:30 PM onwards). Need to decide: attend Parent-Teacher Workshop at daughters' school OR continue after-school tutoring session. Evaluate if tutoring can be rescheduled or delegated.

tasks.title: Arrange grandparents' help for March 26 Science Fair
tasks.description: Husband unavailable (business trip). Contact in-laws to confirm they can help with March 26 daughters' Science Fair event (2:00-3:30 PM). This conflicts with after-school tutoring session - need backup plan for tutoring.

tasks.title: Create multi-week conflict resolution calendar for March
tasks.description: Compile comprehensive calendar showing all teaching obligations vs daughters' commitments for March. Document solutions for each conflict date: March 12 (duty swap with Zhang Hui), March 19 (husband pickup + evaluate tutoring options), March 26 (grandparents help + tutoring delegation). Include all advance action deadlines.

tasks.title: Confirm Chen Jing's March 17 duty swap request before finalizing March 12/19 swaps
tasks.description: Chen Jing can cover March 12 and 19 afternoons, but needs me to cover her March 17 morning duty (9:00-11:00) in exchange. PROBLEM: March 17 has mandatory Grade 10 Curriculum Review Meeting 9:00-11:30 AM. Need to check if this creates an impossible dependency or if there's alternative coverage.

tasks.title: Contact Lin's parents to confirm their March availability (especially late March)
tasks.description: Husband mentioned parents might have medical checkup in late March but date unconfirmed. Need to know their availability for: 1) March 19 afternoon pickup (husband unavailable due to Guangzhou meeting), 2) March 26 afternoon Science Fair attendance (husband has 2:30 PM meeting). This is blocking final decision on daughters' school event attendance confirmation.

tasks.title: Check with Zhou Ming about March 26 morning duty coverage possibility
tasks.description: Chen Jing mentioned Zhou Ming might be able to help with March 26. Need to verify his availability for morning duty coverage so I can attend daughters' Science Fair setup (9 AM-12 PM). This is lower priority than March 19 since morning setup is optional, but afternoon presentation (2-4:30 PM) is mandatory.

tasks.title: Reply to Primary School - confirm March event attendance by March 8 deadline
tasks.description: Primary school requires attendance confirmation by March 8 for: March 19 workshop (2:30-4 PM, mandatory), March 26 Science Fair (afternoon 2-4:30 PM mandatory, morning optional). CANNOT confirm until: 1) Duty swap for March 19 is secured, 2) Family coverage for March 26 afternoon is confirmed. Need to request extension or provide preliminary response.

tasks.title: Calculate expected financial loss for competition registration scenarios
tasks.description: Analyze two scenarios: (1) Register 8-10 preliminary candidates by March 8 at ¥150 each, risk losing ¥150-450 if 1-3 students drop out; (2) Wait until March 10 confirmation, register at ¥250 each, lose ¥800-1000 in discount savings. Need to assess dropout probability based on Coach Wang's assessment and make financial recommendation.

tasks.title: Contact Competition Office about possible deadline extension or refund policy flexibility
tasks.description: Call or email Guangdong Competition Office (competition.office@gdedu.gov.cn, 020-8765-4321) to inquire if: (1) Early registration deadline can be extended 2-3 days to March 10-11, or (2) Partial refund policy available for student withdrawals before March 15. Explain school's selection timeline conflict.

tasks.title: Review Class 10A competition candidates' recent test scores and attendance
tasks.description: Analyze recent performance data for all 8-10 preliminary candidates to estimate probability of each student making final team. Focus on borderline candidates (Zhao Ming, Sun Jie, Wu Dan) and uncertain candidates (Ma Lin, Yang Feng) to assess dropout risk for early registration decision.

tasks.title: Discuss with Math Department Head about budget approval for full-price registration option
tasks.description: If early registration is too risky, discuss with Department Head whether school can approve registering 8-10 students at full price (¥250 each = ¥2000-2500 total) after March 10 confirmation. Current math competition budget is ¥2500, which may not cover full-price registration plus other expenses. May need to request additional Q1 budget or defer some expenses to Q2.

tasks.title: Review upcoming week schedule for conflicts and preparation needs (March 26-April 1)
tasks.description: Conduct weekly schedule preview: check calendar for teaching duties, homeroom supervision, administrative meetings, and family commitments. Cross-reference with duty swap requests, preparation tasks, and daughters' school events. Flag conflicts and identify items requiring advance preparation (student reports, meeting materials, competition materials).

tasks.title: Respond to Chen Jing's March 31 duty swap request
tasks.description: Chen Jing offered to cover March 31 morning homeroom supervision (7:30-8:30 AM) in exchange for April 2 afternoon exam proctoring. Need to check April calendar and confirm if this swap works. This would resolve conflict with daughters' awards ceremony.

tasks.title: Prepare Q1 teaching performance review materials for March 27 meeting
tasks.description: Compile materials for mandatory Q1 Teaching Performance Review Meeting (March 27, 2:00-4:30 PM): Class 10A student performance summary reports, parent engagement metrics from conferences, Q1 teaching objectives achievement review. Need to reference existing student performance notes.

tasks.title: Prepare math competition answer keys and scoring rubrics for March 28 training
tasks.description: Coach Wang requested answer keys and scoring rubrics for final mock competition training session on March 28 (3:30-5:30 PM). Need to review problem sets and create detailed scoring guidelines for 8 competition team students.

tasks.title: Collect final competition registration forms from Wang Zihan and Liu Mei
tasks.description: Need signed parent confirmation forms from Class 10A competition students (Wang Zihan and Liu Mei) by March 27 noon for provincial office submission. Follow up if not received by March 26 afternoon.

tasks.title: Extract and document all competition discount policies from registration email
tasks.description: Review MSG-5021 from Provincial Competition Office and create comprehensive documentation of all discount policies including rates, thresholds, stacking rules, mutual exclusivity constraints, deadlines, and calculation sequence. Need to map out which discounts can combine and which are either-or choices.

tasks.title: Calculate all viable discount combination scenarios for different student counts
tasks.description: Model total costs for 7, 10, and 12 student scenarios with all possible discount combinations: (1) Merit waivers first, (2) Early-Bird vs Institutional, (3) with/without Payment Method discount, (4) with/without Material Bundle. Need to identify minimum-cost configuration for each student count scenario and determine break-even points for adding borderline students.

tasks.title: Determine optimal discount strategy and recommend final student roster
tasks.description: Based on cost calculations (NOTE-114) and Coach Wang's Feb 25 assessment results, decide: (1) Should we pursue Early-Bird (15%, risky, Feb 28 deadline) or Institutional (10%, safe)? (2) Is registering borderline students to hit 8-student or 12-student thresholds cost-effective? (3) Should we use Payment Method discount (5% extra but admin work)? (4) Final recommended student count and total budget. Need to balance cost optimization with student readiness and competition success probability.

tasks.title: Submit merit waiver documentation for Chen Yuxuan and Liu Siqi
tasks.description: Prepare and submit merit-based waiver applications for 2 students who placed top 3 in 2025 provincial competition. Need to gather: (1) Previous year competition certificates, (2) Student ID verification, (3) School participation confirmation letter. Deadline: February 20, 2026. These waivers must be processed first as they affect group discount threshold calculations.

tasks.title: Prepare budget approval requisition with final cost breakdown
tasks.description: Once discount strategy is finalized (after Feb 25 assessment), prepare complete payment requisition for Finance Department including: (1) Official competition notice, (2) Final student roster with parent consent forms, (3) Itemized cost breakdown showing all applied discounts and calculation sequence, (4) Total amount and payment method specification. Must submit by March 8 for March 15 payment deadline. If amount exceeds ¥10,000, allow extra time for VP approval.

tasks.title: Follow up with Coach Wang after Feb 25 assessment for final student recommendations
tasks.description: Contact Coach Wang after the Feb 25 advanced problem set test to get final recommendations on 5 borderline students (Sun Wei, Ma Ling, Xu Hao, Tang Shuyi, Wu Qiang). Need definitive assessment of competition readiness to inform final registration decision. This input is critical for determining whether to register 7, 10, or 12 students total.

tasks.title: Review and update Class 10A mid-term examination preparation schedule
tasks.description: Mid-term exams scheduled March 10-14. Need to coordinate examination paper submission (due March 3), grading timeline, and grade analysis meeting (March 20). Ensure no conflicts with competition registration final deadline (March 15).

tasks.title: Review all seven recommendation letter requests and extract key information
tasks.description: Read emails from Chen Yuxuan, Wang Zihan, Liu Ming, Zhang Lei, Huang Ting, Li Xiao, and Zhou Min. Extract: math grades/percentiles, relationship depth (years known, homeroom vs transfer), application deadlines, program acceptance rates, family background/need indicators, alternative options available.

tasks.title: Build decision matrix for recommendation letter selection across five dimensions
tasks.description: Create structured comparison matrix for seven students: (1) Math performance percentile, (2) Relationship depth score (years known × interaction frequency), (3) Deadline urgency (days remaining), (4) Program competitiveness (acceptance rate - lower = more competitive), (5) Genuine need score (family economic background, alternative options). Normalize scores for comparison.

tasks.title: Apply hard floor constraints to filter recommendation candidates
tasks.description: Exclude students below quality threshold: (1) Math grade below 75th percentile (insufficient for credible strong recommendation), (2) Application deadline less than 10 days away (insufficient time for quality letter given exam prep and teaching load). Document which students are filtered and reasoning.

tasks.title: Perform Pareto dominance analysis on remaining candidates
tasks.description: Among students passing hard constraints, identify Pareto frontier: students not dominated on all five dimensions (academic merit, relationship depth, urgency, program competitiveness, genuine need). Document dominated vs non-dominated students with specific dimension comparisons.

tasks.title: Rank Pareto frontier candidates using values-driven dimension weights
tasks.description: Apply Lin's teaching philosophy weights to Pareto frontier students: Academic merit 35%, Genuine need 30%, Relationship depth 25%, Urgency 10%, Program competitiveness (tie-breaker only). Calculate weighted scores reflecting rural background values and commitment to educational equity. Select top three students for recommendation letters.

tasks.title: Draft respectful decline messages for four students not selected
tasks.description: Write personalized, constructive decline emails to students not selected for recommendation letters. Acknowledge their strengths, explain capacity constraints honestly, provide alternative guidance (other teachers, program options, future opportunities). Maintain supportive homeroom teacher relationship.

tasks.title: Schedule recommendation letter writing blocks around exam preparation
tasks.description: Block out 3-hour focused writing sessions for three recommendation letters. Schedule between March 3-12, avoiding senior teacher certification exam prep time (March 5-14 evenings) and teaching duties. Each letter requires ~2-3 hours for quality personalized content.

tasks.title: Prepare for Grade 10 Mathematics Department curriculum review meeting
tasks.description: Review Q1 teaching materials and student performance data for upcoming curriculum committee meeting. Prepare feedback on current textbook effectiveness and suggestions for Q2 adjustments.

tasks.title: Contact Liu Yan (Li Jie's mother) to schedule urgent parent meeting
tasks.description: Li Jie's mother is very concerned about his math performance drop (rank 10 to 28). Need to schedule meeting today or tomorrow, review his mid-term exam analysis, and prepare explanation of performance factors. Phone: 138-2345-6789. Consider checking Li Jie's recent homework completion and class participation records before meeting.

tasks.title: Submit semester teaching plan to Academic Affairs by Feb 20
tasks.description: Prepare and submit Spring 2026 semester teaching plan including: weekly schedule with chapter breakdown, assessment plan (quiz/exam dates), supplementary materials list, and Class 10A homeroom activity calendar. Submit via Academic Affairs portal before Thursday deadline.

tasks.title: Confirm Provincial Math Competition team roster by Feb 22
tasks.description: Log into competition portal and submit final confirmation of 8-student team roster with ID numbers and competition track selections. Must complete by Feb 22 to maintain 40% early-bird discount eligibility. Coordinate with Coach Wang if needed to finalize borderline student selections.

tasks.title: Respond to Chen Jing's duty swap request for Feb 25
tasks.description: Chen Jing needs coverage for Feb 25 afternoon duty (2:00-5:30 PM) due to mother-in-law's surgery. Check calendar for conflicts with daughters' events and confirm if can swap. If yes, propose early March date for her to cover in return (possibly March 19 or 26 when daughters have school events).

tasks.title: Decide on transportation method for February 15 Guangzhou workshop
tasks.description: Choose between high-speed rail (¥150 round-trip, 2.5 hours total) or intercity bus (¥60 round-trip, 4.5 hours total). Consider: daughters' homework help timing (3-4 hours needed, 3-7 PM optimal), parent meeting prep deadline (Sunday 8 PM), husband available only after 3 PM. High-speed rail allows return by 6:30 PM for evening homework help; bus returns by 8:30 PM missing critical homework time. Evaluate ¥90 cost difference against family time value and Monday meeting preparation quality.

tasks.title: Review February household budget - competition expenses impact
tasks.description: Check recent competition-related expenditures (January registration fees, workshop materials) against monthly budget. Assess affordability of ¥90 transportation upgrade. Monthly salary ~¥6000, ¥90 = 1.5%. Review if recent competition expenses create financial constraint for choosing faster transportation option.

tasks.title: Prepare Class 10A parent meeting materials - all 35 students
tasks.description: Complete individual progress reports, class summary presentation, semester goals, and parent feedback forms. Must be submitted by Monday February 16 at 8:00 PM. Requires 4-5 hours of focused work. Schedule depends on Saturday workshop return time - earlier return allows Sunday afternoon/evening work; late return forces rushed Sunday evening preparation.

tasks.title: Book transportation tickets for February 15 Guangzhou trip
tasks.description: Once decision is made, book either high-speed rail tickets (Shenzhen North to Guangzhou South, depart ~7:30 AM, return ~5:30 PM) or intercity bus tickets (Luohu to Tianhe, depart ~6:00 AM, return ~5:30 PM). Book early to ensure seat availability.

tasks.title: Calculate net cost for all three competition registration payment paths
tasks.description: Analyze Path 1 (purchase order with 15% discount, ¥3,060 net after discount), Path 2 (personal credit card ¥3,600 with 8% cashback but no reimbursement), and Path 3 (prepaid account ¥3,600 direct debit). Factor in reimbursement timeline, year-end bonus probability, and personal financial risk. Current prepaid balance is ¥2,300 (insufficient for Path 3). Must complete analysis before March 15 registration deadline.

tasks.title: Confirm prepaid account balance and year-end spending threshold with Finance Office
tasks.description: Verify current prepaid account balance (¥2,300 as stated in email) and confirm department's year-to-date spending status relative to ¥12,000 threshold for ¥500 year-end bonus. Need to understand if combined competition expenses from all four teachers (¥10,350 total) will forfeit bonus eligibility. Contact finance.reimbursement@szexperimental.edu.cn.

tasks.title: Coordinate with Zhang Hui, Teacher Wang, and Teacher Liu about shared competition payment strategy
tasks.description: Discuss combined departmental spending impact with other three teachers planning competition registrations (total ¥6,750 from their teams). Current projection shows combined expenses would exceed ¥12,000 threshold, forfeiting year-end bonus. Teacher Wang mentioned flexibility to use personal payment. Need to coordinate overall department strategy before individual payment decisions. Registration deadline March 15.

tasks.title: Submit purchase order for competition registration if selected as optimal path
tasks.description: If Path 1 (purchase order) is determined to have lowest net cost to department, submit purchase order form to finance office for 8 Class 10A students (¥3,600 gross, ¥3,060 net after 15% institutional discount). Finance confirmed 45-day processing timeline will complete before fiscal year end. Must submit by March 15 registration deadline.

tasks.title: URGENT: Analyze March 18 commitment overlap crisis and develop remediation strategy
tasks.description: Schedule change compressed three critical commitments into overlapping March 18 time slots: (1) After-school tutoring for Wang Zihan, Li Hua, Chen Ming 4:30-6:00 PM, (2) Daughters' mandatory field trip orientation 3:00-5:00 PM, (3) Cover Zhang Hui's homeroom duty 3:30-5:30 PM. Must map cascading consequences, assess violation costs, and implement immediate remediation actions.

tasks.title: Contact husband about attending daughters' March 18 field trip orientation as backup
tasks.description: Explore whether husband can attend the mandatory parent-volunteer orientation on March 18, 3:00-5:00 PM at primary school on my behalf. Need to confirm his work schedule flexibility and willingness. This would preserve daughters' field trip participation while allowing me to fulfill teaching commitments.

tasks.title: Identify substitute teacher for Zhang Hui's March 18 homeroom duty coverage
tasks.description: Find another colleague who can cover Class 10B homeroom supervision 3:30-5:30 PM on March 18, since I have overlapping commitments. Contact Zhou Ming or Chen Jing to see if they have availability. Explain Zhang Hui's family emergency situation.

tasks.title: Communicate proactively with Wang Xiaoming, Li Fang, and Chen Ming's parents about potential tutoring reschedule
tasks.description: Draft email explaining schedule conflict situation and propose alternative solutions: reschedule one session to March 17 evening or extend March 19-20 sessions. Emphasize commitment to helping students despite unexpected schedule changes. Must send before parents hear about conflicts through other channels.

tasks.title: Prepare midterm exam review materials for Class 10A
tasks.description: Compile practice problems and review sheets for Class 10A midterm exam covering calculus, probability, and geometry topics. Distribute to all students by March 19.

tasks.title: Extract 2025 competition transaction records and calculate total sunk costs
tasks.description: Pull finance records for 2025 Provincial Math Competition: initial registration transaction (March 2025, ¥2,250 for 15 students) and refund denial documentation (May 2025, ¥450 non-refundable loss from 3 dropouts). Confirm exact amounts and dates for budget justification report to Academic Affairs.

tasks.title: Calculate expected cost per participant for both registration strategies
tasks.description: Create detailed cost-benefit analysis comparing: (1) Early registration at ¥150/student with 20% expected dropout rate vs. (2) Regular registration at ¥250/student with 5% expected dropout rate. Include effective cost per successful participant, total budget impact, and risk assessment. Use 2025 actual data as baseline for dropout projections.

tasks.title: Submit budget justification report to Academic Affairs Office
tasks.description: Prepare comprehensive report for Academic Affairs including: (1) 2025 dropout analysis with root causes, (2) Proposed 2026 registration strategy (early vs. regular) with cost-benefit calculations, (3) Risk mitigation measures (commitment screening, mid-cycle reviews, parent agreements), (4) Expected cost per successful participant comparison. Due March 20, 2026.

tasks.title: Email competition office about refund policy clarifications for 2026
tasks.description: Follow up with Guangdong Provincial Education Department Competition Office to confirm: (1) Are refund policies identical to 2025? (2) Is there any partial refund option for medical/family emergencies? (3) Can student substitutions help recover costs if done before April 1? Document responses for decision-making.

tasks.title: Finalize 2026 competition registration decision and execute
tasks.description: Based on cost-benefit analysis, Coach Wang consultation, and Academic Affairs feedback, make final decision on registration strategy. tasks.title: Coordinate with husband for daughters' April 14 and April 18 event coverage
tasks.description: Two daughters' school events conflict with work commitments: April 14 morning art exhibition (overlaps with Math proctoring) and April 18 morning safety workshop (overlaps with Physics proctoring). tasks.title: Coordinate with Coach Wang for equipment delegation contingency plan
tasks.description: If April 16 duty swap fails, may need to delegate TI-Nspire calculator distribution to Coach Wang for April 15 training session. Do NOT execute until duty swap status is confirmed.

tasks.title: Submit finalized proctoring preference form to Academic Affairs by April 10 deadline
tasks.description: Academic Affairs requires proctoring preference adjustment form submission by April 10. This is the final step after resolving all conflicts: (1) duty swap confirmations must be complete, (2) family coverage must be confirmed, (3) equipment delegation decision must be finalized. Document final exam week schedule with all confirmed arrangements.

response_body.subject: Re: Calculator Purchase Decision - Account Status and Policy Clarification
response_body.body:
Dear Teacher Lin,

Thank you for your inquiry. Here are the answers to your questions:

1. **Prepaid account balance**: ¥3,250 currently available (as of March 28 verification). This is sufficient to cover the ¥4,680 final payment if we process it as a department purchase.

2. **Year-end spending threshold**: Both scenarios count toward the ¥12,000 threshold:
   - Early-bird option: ¥5,480 total (deposit already counted)
   - Flash sale option: ¥4,896 total (but the ¥800 deposit loss still counts as spent)
   - Net difference in threshold impact: ¥584 (¥5,480 vs ¥4,896)
   - However, the abandoned deposit (¥800) remains on our books as a sunk cost

3. **Payment processing**: The early-bird final payment can be processed directly from the prepaid account if you submit a purchase requisition form by April 2 noon. We can expedite approval given the deadline.

4. **Reimbursement timeline**: If you pay personally, reimbursement takes 15-20 business days after submission with proper receipts.

**Additional consideration**: Switching vendors means the ¥800 deposit becomes a permanent loss to the department budget, even though the flash sale's total cost is lower. The actual budget impact comparison:
- Early-bird total cost: ¥5,480 (includes training materials + priority support)
- Flash sale total cost: ¥4,896 + ¥800 sunk deposit = ¥5,696 actual budget impact

From a pure budget perspective, completing the early-bird program is more efficient.

Please let me know if you need the expedited purchase requisition form.

Best regards,
Zhao Min
Finance Office
Shenzhen Experimental High School

I am writing regarding my existing order (deposit payment TXN-6021, March 15, 2026) for 12 TI-84 Plus CE graphing calculators.

I have received a competing flash sale offer at ¥398/unit (¥4,896 total including shipping for 12 units), which is ¥584 lower than your program's total cost of ¥5,480.

I greatly value your program's bundled training materials and priority technical support, which the competing vendor does not offer. However, given our school's budget constraints, I must consider the cost difference carefully.

Before the final payment deadline (April 3), I would like to request:

I prefer to continue with your program due to the superior support and training materials, but I need to justify the cost difference to our finance office.

The competing offer expires April 2 at 23:59, so I would appreciate your response by tomorrow afternoon if possible.

Thank you for your consideration.

Best regards,
Lin Jia Hui

response_body.subject: Urgent: Duty Swap Request for April Exam Week - Proctoring Coverage Needed
response_body.body:
Dear Chen Jing,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to request your assistance with a critical scheduling conflict during our upcoming April mid-term exam week.

I have been assigned to proctor the Math Paper 1 exam on April 7 (Tuesday, 9:00-11:00 AM), but my twin daughters have a mandatory art exhibition opening at their primary school during the exact same time slot. This is a milestone event where their artwork will be featured, and parent attendance is required and cannot be rescheduled.

After reviewing our past duty swap history, I note that you have been very reliable in similar situations. Would you be able to cover my proctoring duty on April 7? In exchange, I can offer:

1. Coverage for your proctoring duty on April 10 (Friday, 2:00-4:00 PM) if needed
2. Take on your next grading session coordination duty
3. Any other reciprocal arrangement that works for your schedule

I have calculated my work-family balance over the past 4 weeks and found I have prioritized work commitments 78% of the time when conflicts arose. This daughters' event represents an irreplaceable family milestone that I cannot miss.

Please let me know your availability at your earliest convenience. I would greatly appreciate your support.

Best regards,
Lin Jia Hui

response_body.body:
Dear Zhang Hui,

I hope this message finds you well. I've just reviewed the April duty roster and my daughters' school calendar, and I'm facing two critical conflicts that require your help:

1. **April 8 (Wednesday)** - Evening Study Hall duty (18:00-20:30)
   Conflict: Mandatory parent-teacher conference at daughters' school (14:00-17:00)
   My concern: Even if the conference ends at 17:00, I may not make it back in time for the 18:00 duty start, especially with traffic.

2. **April 18 (Saturday)** - Campus Patrol duty (16:00-18:00) during mid-term exam week
   Conflict: Mandatory Safety Drill parent volunteer day at daughters' school (09:00-11:30)
   My concern: This is marked as MANDATORY with at least one parent required. My husband has a critical client presentation that day.

- Any of your April duties (I see you have Evening Study Hall April 21-23 and Campus Patrol April 19-20)

Please let me know your availability as soon as possible. I really appreciate your understanding and support.

Best regards,

I heard through the department grapevine about the budget freeze situation - what terrible timing for you with the competition prep starting soon!

I wanted to reach out because I have 6 TI-Nspire calculators from last year's competition cohort. My current group only has 4 students this cycle, so I have 2 units that are essentially sitting unused.

If you're looking at equipment sharing as an option, I'm happy to coordinate a lending arrangement. However, I should mention:

1. My competition prep sessions run Tuesday/Thursday 4-6pm in Room 302
2. I'd need the calculators back by April 25 for our regional mock exam
3. Two of my students (including Wang Zihan) sometimes need extra practice time on weekends

Also, Teacher Liu from Grade 11 mentioned she has 3-4 older TI-84 Plus models that might work for basic practice, though they're not as advanced as the Nspire series.

Let me know if you want to discuss logistics. I know how stressful these last-minute pivots can be, especially with parent commitments already made.

Best,
Zhang Hui

P.S. - Are we still on for the March duty swap arrangement? I haven't heard back about the final confirmation.

response_body.subject: Re: Budget Freeze - Impact on Your Calculator Order?
response_body.body:
Jia Hui,

I saw the Finance Office announcement yesterday and immediately thought of your competition equipment order. Didn't you mention the calculators were on a payment deadline?

This freeze timing is terrible - I know Coach Wang has been pushing to start intensive training sessions next week. Have you checked whether competition equipment falls under the emergency exemption category?

I remember Vice Principal Chen approved a similar exception last year when the chemistry lab had a vendor deadline conflict during the mid-year audit. It required a lot of paperwork though.

Let me know if you need help navigating this. I can ask Zhou Ming if he's dealt with emergency exception requests before.

Chen Jing
Math Department

response_body.subject: Re: Urgent: Duty Swap Request for April Exam Week - Confirmed
response_body.body:
Dear Jia Hui,

Of course I can help! I completely understand the importance of being present for your daughters' art exhibition. These milestone moments are irreplaceable.

I am available to cover your Math Paper 1 proctoring duty on April 7 (9:00-11:00 AM). No need for immediate reciprocity - we can work out the details later. Your offer to cover my April 10 duty would actually be helpful, as I have a dental appointment that afternoon.

Please go ahead and enjoy the art exhibition with your daughters. They will remember your presence there.

I'll coordinate with the exam office to update the proctoring roster.

Best,
Chen Jing

response_body.subject: April Competition Team Coaching Sessions - Need Your Availability ASAP
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

I need to finalize the April competition team coaching schedule by April 8 to reserve the lab rooms and notify students.

For the intensive pre-provincial competition training, I'm planning 4-5 sessions during April 14-18 (exam week). I know this is tight timing, but the provincial competition is April 26, and we need maximum preparation time.

Could you confirm your availability for co-coaching sessions? Ideally:
- Two evening sessions (6:00-8:00 PM) - April 14 and 16
- Two afternoon sessions (4:00-6:00 PM) - April 15 and 17
- One weekend session (Sunday April 19, 2:00-5:00 PM)

I understand exam week is complicated with proctoring and grading duties. If you can only commit to 2-3 sessions, please let me know which ones work best.

The students are counting on us, and several parents have already asked about the training schedule.

Please reply by April 7 if possible.

Best regards,
Coach Wang

response_body.subject: Re: April Mid-term Exam Week - Make-up Exam Proctoring Duty Assignment Request
response_body.body:
Dear Academic Affairs Office,

Thank you for the proctoring assignment request. After reviewing my April exam week commitments, I can confirm my availability for:

Option A: Thursday, April 9, 2026, 14:00-16:00, Exam Hall C (Building 3, 2F)

This is the only slot that does not conflict with my existing duties:
- Option B conflicts with competition coaching session (April 10, 09:00-11:30, Building 1)
- Option C conflicts with Grade 10 grading session (April 11, 09:00-11:30, same building)

Option A works well as it follows my Class 10A exam material preparation block in the morning and does not require cross-building travel that would compress my preparation time.

I will arrive at 13:45 for the pre-exam briefing as required.

Best regards,
Lin Jia Hui

response_body.subject: Request for Grading Session Coverage - April 8
response_body.body:
Dear Zhang Hui,

I am reaching out regarding the grading session coordination scheduled for April 8 (Wednesday, 2:00-5:00 PM). I have a conflict with my daughters' science project presentation at their primary school (3:00-4:30 PM), which is a mandatory parent attendance event.

Given our successful collaboration on duty swaps in March, I wanted to ask if you would be available to coordinate the grading session in my place, or if we could adjust the timing to start at 5:00 PM instead?

I can offer to take on additional responsibilities:
- Cover any of your April proctoring duties
- Lead the next department curriculum review meeting
- Assist with your Class 10B parent communications

This science presentation is a significant milestone for my daughters, and the timing unfortunately cannot be changed by the primary school.

Please let me know if this arrangement would work for you.

Thank you for your understanding,
Lin Jia Hui

response_body.subject: Re: April 15-17 Schedule - Still Waiting on Project Assignment
response_body.body:
Hi Jia Hui,

I know you need to finalize your exam week schedule, but I still don't have clarity on my work situation for mid-April.

My manager mentioned a potential client site visit April 14-16, but hasn't confirmed yet. He said he'll know by April 7 at the earliest. If that happens, I definitely can't help with the girls' school events those days.

I can probably handle April 17 morning if needed, but April 15 afternoon is uncertain right now.

Can your parents help as backup? I know you wanted to avoid asking them again after they covered for us in March, but this might be unavoidable.

Sorry I can't give you a definite answer yet. I'll push my manager for clarity early next week.

Love,
[Husband]

response_body.subject: Delegation Request: Competition Coaching Session - April 9
response_body.body:
Dear Coach Wang,

I hope you are doing well. I am writing to request your assistance with delegating the competition team coaching session scheduled for April 9 (Thursday, 4:00-6:00 PM).

Due to a mandatory parent safety workshop at my daughters' primary school (4:30-6:00 PM on the same day), I will be unable to lead the session. Given your expertise and familiarity with our competition students, I believe you would be the ideal person to cover this session.

I have prepared the following materials for the session:
- Practice problem sets (Provincial Competition level)
- Student roster with current progress notes
- Answer keys and solution strategies
- Individual student feedback forms

The session focus is on geometry proofs and combinatorics problems. I can meet with you on April 3 or 4 to review the materials and discuss any specific student needs.

This is part of a broader work-family conflict resolution during exam week, and I have carefully assessed that this coaching session can be effectively delegated while my daughters' school events cannot be replicated.

Please let me know if you are available to take on this session.

With gratitude,
Lin Jia Hui

response_body.subject: Re: April Exam Week Duty Swap Inquiry - Need Your Availability First
response_body.body:
Hi Jia Hui,

I received your inquiry about potentially swapping proctoring duties during April exam week. I'm happy to help if our schedules align.

However, I need to know which specific time slots you need coverage for before I can confirm whether I can swap. My availability depends on:
- Which sessions you're assigned to (morning vs afternoon, specific days)
- Whether the swap would be a direct exchange or if I'm just covering for you

Could you let me know your proctoring assignment once you finalize it? I know you mentioned some family scheduling uncertainties. I have some flexibility on April 15 and 17 afternoons, but April 14 and 16 are difficult for me.

Also, have you confirmed with the grading schedule yet? If we swap proctoring, it might affect the grading session assignments too.

Let me know once you have more clarity on your end!

Best,
Chen Jing

response_body.subject: Urgent: Duty Swap Request for April 7 & 9 - Exam Week Conflicts
response_body.body:
Hi Zhang Hui,

I hope this message finds you well. I'm facing a difficult situation with the compressed exam schedule and need your help.

The schedule change has created two conflicts with my daughters' mandatory school events:

1. April 7 (Tuesday) 14:00-16:00 - I'm assigned proctoring duty in Room 302, but there's a mandatory parent safety workshop at my daughters' school 14:30-16:30. Could you possibly cover this afternoon slot for me?

2. April 9 (Thursday) 8:00-10:00 - I'm assigned morning proctoring in Room 405, but there's a parent-teacher conference at my daughters' school 8:30-11:30. This one is particularly important as it's their spring semester review.

I know you helped me with the March 12 swap (which I really appreciated!), and I still owe you coverage from that. I can take any of your duties during the exam week that don't conflict with my remaining assignments, or I can cover for you during the May exam makeup sessions.

I understand this is very short notice with the schedule compression. If you can't help with both, even one would make a huge difference. Please let me know as soon as possible - the swap deadline is April 5.

Thank you so much for considering this.

Best regards,
Jia Hui

response_body.subject: Re: April Events Schedule - Final Confirmation Needed for Twin Daughters
response_body.body:
Dear Ms. Lin,

Thank you for your inquiry about the April event schedule for your daughters.

We understand you need final confirmation for planning purposes. Unfortunately, we are still waiting for district approval on two events:

1. Spring Arts Performance (tentatively April 15, 2:00-4:30 PM) - Parent attendance MANDATORY
2. Science Project Exhibition (tentatively April 17, 9:00 AM-12:00 PM) - Parent volunteer participation strongly encouraged

We expect district approval by April 7-8, but cannot guarantee earlier confirmation. Both events require parent participation as they are part of the district's family engagement initiative.

We apologize for the uncertainty and will notify you as soon as we receive confirmation.

Best regards,
Primary School Administration Office

response_body.subject: Competition Team Selection - Final Decision Needed by April 5
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

Based on the March selection tests, I've compiled performance rankings for all 18 candidates. We need to finalize the 12-student roster by April 5 to meet the provincial registration deadline (April 10).

Top performers are clear: Wang Zihan, Liu Chen, and Zhang Ming are definite selections. However, positions 10-15 are very close in scores. I recommend we meet April 3 afternoon to discuss the borderline cases, especially considering:

- Student commitment level (dropout risk assessment based on your 2025 experience)
- Parent support and transportation logistics
- Balance between competition focus and regular coursework

After we finalize, you'll need to send formal notification letters to parents and coordinate training schedules.

Let me know if April 3, 15:30 works for you.

Coach Wang

{"message_id": "MSG-5189", "from": "lin.jiahui@szexperimental.edu.cn", "to": "zhang.hui@szexperimental.edu.cn", "subject": "Urgent: Duty Swap Request for April 7 & 9 - Exam Week Conflicts", "date": "2026-04-03T16:45:00+08:00", "body": "Hi Zhang Hui,

response_body.subject: Competition Training Schedule - April 14-18 Critical Sessions
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

Following up on our discussion about the provincial competition preparation timeline. The week of April 14-18 includes several critical training sessions that cannot be easily rescheduled:

Tuesday April 15, 14:00-17:00: Advanced geometry problem-solving workshop (5 Class 10A students attending: Zhang Wei, Liu Ying, Chen Ming, Wang Zihan, Li Xiao)

Thursday April 17, 08:00-11:00: Mock competition simulation test (full team, 12 students total)

Please let me know your availability once you've reviewed the exam proctoring roster.

Best regards,
Coach Wang
Mathematics Competition Team

response_body.subject: April Exam Week - Potential Duty Swap Discussion
response_body.body:
Hi Jia Hui,

I saw the exam proctoring roster email and wanted to reach out early. I have a medical appointment scheduled for Wednesday April 15 afternoon that I cannot reschedule (specialist appointment booked 3 months ago).

If you're planning to select the Wednesday April 15 afternoon Physics session (Session 2B), would you be interested in swapping? I could cover any Monday or Friday session for you in exchange.

Thanks,
Chen Jing

response_body.subject: Request to Excuse Absence - Family Emergency
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

I am writing to inform you that Liu Ting will need to be absent from school on April 7-8 due to a family emergency. Her grandmother in Guangzhou is hospitalized and we need to travel there to visit her.

Liu Ting is very concerned about missing classes, especially mathematics. Would it be possible for her to get the lesson materials and homework assignments in advance so she can study during the trip?

We will ensure she catches up on all missed work when she returns on April 9.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Liu Ting's Father
Class 10A Parent

response_body.subject: FINAL REMINDER: Provincial Math Competition Registration Confirmation Due April 5
response_body.body:
Dear Teacher Lin Jia Hui,

This is the final reminder that registration confirmation for the 2026 Guangdong Provincial Mathematics Competition must be received by April 5, 2026, 11:59 PM.

Your preliminary registration (submitted March 18) included:
- School: Shenzhen Experimental High School
- Proposed team size: 8-12 students
- Category: High School Division
- Status: PENDING CONFIRMATION

To finalize registration, you must:
1. Submit final student roster with names and student IDs
2. Confirm payment of registration fees (¥150 per student)
3. Acknowledge competition rules and supervision requirements
4. Provide emergency contact information for competition day

Failure to confirm by April 5 will result in:
- Automatic cancellation of preliminary registration
- Loss of reserved competition slots
- Ineligibility for late registration (no exceptions)

The competition will be held on May 18, 2026. Confirmed schools will receive detailed logistics information by April 15.

Please submit confirmation through the provincial competition portal or reply to this email with required information.

If you need to withdraw your registration, please notify us immediately so we can allocate slots to waitlisted schools.

Best regards,
Competition Coordination Office
Guangdong Provincial Education Department
Phone: +86 20-8765-4321

response_body.subject: Mandatory Parent Participation Events - April Mid-month Schedule
response_body.body:
Dear Parents of Grade 3 Students,

We are pleased to announce three important parent participation events during the week of April 14-18:

1. Spring Art Exhibition Opening Ceremony
   Date: Tuesday, April 14, 9:00-11:30 AM
   Location: School Art Gallery, Building A
   Your daughters' artwork will be featured in the Grade 3 exhibition. Parent attendance is mandatory as students will present their work.

2. Spring Concert Dress Rehearsal (Parent Observers Required)
   Date: Thursday, April 16, 2:00-4:30 PM
   Location: School Auditorium
   Parents must attend to provide feedback and costume adjustments before the final performance on April 20.

3. Campus Safety Workshop for Parents
   Date: Saturday, April 18, 8:30-11:00 AM
   Location: Multi-purpose Hall
   Mandatory attendance required by district education bureau policy. Topics include emergency response procedures and student pickup protocols.

Please confirm your attendance by replying to this email by April 7. If you cannot attend, you must designate an alternative family member and provide their contact information.

Thank you for your cooperation.

Luohu District Primary School Administration Office

response_body.subject: Urgent: Request for Meeting About Zhang Lei's Math Performance
response_body.body:
Lin Teacher,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing regarding my son Zhang Lei's recent performance in mathematics. His mid-term exam score dropped significantly from 88 to 72, and I'm very concerned about this trend.

I noticed that he seems to have difficulty with the trigonometry unit we just finished. Could we schedule an individual meeting this week to discuss his learning situation and what we can do at home to support his improvement?

I am available any afternoon after 4:00 PM this week except Thursday. Please let me know what time works best for you.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,
Zhang Hui
Parent of Zhang Lei, Class 10A

response_body.subject: Classroom Behavior Concern - Wang Zihan
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

I received a note from Wang Zihan's desk mate's parent mentioning that Zihan has been talking frequently during class and sometimes distracts other students during mathematics lessons.

This is quite unlike him - he has always been focused and respectful in class. I'm wondering if something has changed recently or if there are any issues at school that might be affecting his behavior.

I would appreciate your observation and feedback on this matter. If you think it's necessary, I'm happy to come in for a meeting to discuss how we can address this together.

Thank you for your attention.

Best regards,
Wang Xiaoming
Parent of Wang Zihan, Class 10A

response_body.title: Emergency Budget Exception Request Procedures (Form FIN-2026-EX)
response_body.content:
# Emergency Budget Exception Request Procedures

## Overview
Emergency budget exceptions allow departments to proceed with time-sensitive payments during budget freeze periods when institutional interests are at risk.

## Eligibility Criteria
Exception requests are considered for:
- Contractual penalty clauses (late fees, liquidated damages)
- Non-refundable deposit forfeiture (≥¥500)
- Critical operational disruption (safety, essential services)
- Vendor relationship preservation (long-term institutional partnerships)

## Exclusions
- Convenience purchases (non-critical timing)
- Discretionary spending (can be deferred without institutional harm)
- Personal preference items

## Request Process
1. Complete Form FIN-2026-EX (available: Finance Office or staff portal)
2. Attach supporting documentation:
   - Vendor contract with relevant clauses highlighted
   - Institutional impact assessment (operational, financial, reputational)
   - Alternative resolution attempts (vendor negotiation records)
   - Department head written endorsement
3. Submit to Vice Principal's office (chen.weimin@szexperimental.edu.cn)
4. Vice Principal reviews and forwards to District Finance Officer if approved

## Approval Timeline
- Standard processing: 2-3 business days
- Expedited processing (extreme urgency): 24-48 hours (requires Vice Principal discretion)
- Dual approval required: Vice Principal + District Finance Officer

## Historical Precedents
- Chemistry Lab equipment (2025): Approved - vendor deadline during mid-year audit
- Library software renewal (2024): Denied - no contractual penalty, deferrable
- Sports equipment (2025): Approved - provincial competition deadline, non-refundable deposit

## Notes
- Exception approval does NOT waive budget accountability
- Approved exceptions are included in next quarter's budget reconciliation
- Repeated exception requests may trigger departmental budget review

## Contact
Finance Office: ext. 8201 | liu.mei@szexperimental.edu.cn

SHENZHEN EXPERIMENTAL HIGH SCHOOL - PROCUREMENT POLICY

**VENDOR VERIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**

All equipment purchases exceeding ¥5,000 must use vendors from the approved vendor list OR complete new vendor verification process.

**New Vendor Verification Process:**
1. Submit vendor information form to Finance Office
2. Provide: business license, tax registration, bank account details
3. Minimum 2 reference letters from other educational institutions
4. Finance Office conducts background check
5. Processing time: 5 business days minimum
6. Approval required from Finance Director for vendors >¥10,000

**Approved Vendor List:**
Maintained by Finance Office, updated quarterly
Access: www.szexperimental.edu.cn/finance/vendors
Contact: Equipment Procurement Officer (wang.jian@szexperimental.edu.cn)

**Emergency Procurement:**
For urgent needs, contact Finance Office for expedited review (2-3 business days possible with justification)

**Payment Terms:**
- Deposits: Maximum 20% of order value
- Balance: Due upon delivery confirmation
- All payments processed through school finance system
- Direct vendor payments by staff require reimbursement approval

**Budget Constraints:**
- Quarterly budgets must be committed by 10th day of following quarter
- Uncommitted funds reallocated to general reserves
- Budget transfers between departments require Director approval

Last updated: September 2025

3. **Verify the vendor is on the approved vendor list** with Wang Jian (procurement). Orders >¥5,000 require an approved vendor or a 5-day new-vendor verification (KB-401).
4. **Do not pay personally / from the prepaid account without written finance approval.**

### De-risk April 15 regardless of the vendor outcome
- You have a lead on **10 TI-Nspire units already approved** (PO submitted Mar 26, approved Mar 28, TXN-6032). **Verify actual inventory on hand** with department storage — if real, you only need a bridge for ~2 units.
- **Coach Wang explicitly offered to take over calculator distribution** and receive equipment at his office (C-412) (MSG-5202). Accept that as the contingency; it removes the Apr 15 distribution dependency from your conflict-heavy day.
- Treat the `zhang.hui@business.cn` "I have 6 calculators to lend" offer (MSG-5153) as **unverified** — that address is a parent contact, not your math-department colleague (who uses `@szexperimental.edu.cn`). Coordinate any sharing only through official school channels.

**Cost note:** true budget impact — EarlyBird ¥5,480 vs flash-sale ¥4,896 + ¥800 sunk deposit = **¥5,696**. EarlyBird is cheaper in real budget terms and includes materials, so completing it is the right call *if* the exception is approved.

---

## 2) Exam week — resolve the contradiction first

You have two conflicting "final" schedules from Academic Affairs:

- **Version A — Apr 14–18** (MSG-5199, and MSG-5084 for Class 10A): proctoring Apr 14 AM, Apr 16 PM, Apr 18 AM; mandatory grading Apr 15 PM, Apr 17 AM, Apr 19 AM.
- **Version B — compressed Apr 7–10** (MSG-5187, "due to provincial inspection Apr 18"): proctoring Apr 7 PM, Apr 9 AM + evening, Apr 10 PM.

Version B has internal weekday errors (it calls Apr 7 "Monday" and Apr 10 "Thursday," when Apr 7 is Tuesday), which is a credibility flag. **Call Academic Affairs and get a written confirmation of which schedule is effective before submitting swaps** — otherwise you'll swap against the wrong roster. The Apr 14–18 version is the one that aligns with "mid-month" and the Apr 15 training, so I've mapped conflicts to that below.

## 3) The overlapping commitments (Apr 14–18)

| Date/time | Your work duty | Daughters' school | Verdict | Recommended coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tue Apr 14, 09:00–11:00** | Proctor Math Paper 1 (Hall B) | **Art Exhibition Opening 09:00–11:30 — MANDATORY** | **Hard conflict** | Swap proctoring: Zhou Ming (free Apr 14–15) or Zhang Hui (prefers mornings). Backup: husband/grandparent at the school. |
| **Wed Apr 15, 14:00–17:00** | Math grading calibration — MANDATORY | Arts Festival 14:00–16:30 (**tentative**, approval Apr 7–8) | Potential | Wait for confirmation; if confirmed, husband/grandparent. **Delegate calculator distribution to Coach Wang.** |
| **Thu Apr 16, 14:00–16:00** | Proctor English (Hall C) | **Concert Dress Rehearsal 14:00–16:30 — MANDATORY** | **Hard conflict** | Swap with Chen Jing — she's free Apr 16–17 and wants you to cover **Apr 22, 14:00–16:00** in return (MSG-5084). Ask today. |
| **Fri Apr 17, 09:00–12:00** | Cross-class grading planning — MANDATORY | Science Exhibition 09:00–12:00 (**volunteer, tentative**) | Soft | Husband can probably cover (he said Apr 17 AM); confirm. |
| **Sat Apr 18, 08:30–10:30** | Proctor Physics (Hall A) | **Campus Safety Workshop 08:30–11:00 — MANDATORY** | **Hard conflict** | Swap with Zhang Hui (fully available, prefers mornings). Backup: grandparent. |

Also note **Apr 15 training time is inconsistent** across emails (15:00–17:30 vs 16:00–18:00) and **Apr 17 session time** (08:00–11:00 vs 16:00–18:00) — ask Coach Wang to confirm in writing. And the **provincial competition date** appears as Apr 25/26 *and* May 18; likely preliminary round late April, finals May 18, but confirm.

If Version B (Apr 7–10) turns out to be the live schedule, the same pattern shifts a week earlier — Apr 7 art opening, Apr 8 parent-teacher + science presentation, Apr 9 morning/afternoon events, Apr 10 safety workshop all collide with proctoring/grading/coaching. We'd re-map it once Academic Affairs confirms.

## 4) Deadlines in the next 72 hours

- **Today, Apr 4 (Sat):** Q1 budget report + Q1 expenditure report to Finance; file FIN-2026-EX. (Email-submit tonight so it's timestamped — the office may be closed on a Saturday.)
- **Apr 5 (Sun):** mid-term grade submission; proctoring preferences; **competition roster + registration confirmation (¥150/student)**; proctoring swap requests (per MSG-5084; MSG-5199 allows Apr 10, use the earlier date to be safe); vendor delay/cancellation notification.
- **Apr 7:** primary-school attendance confirmations; Coach Wang's availability.
- **Apr 10:** proctoring preference adjustment deadline; Q1 teaching-quality reports.
- **Apr 15:** calculator distribution / training.
- **Apr 19:** final grading & score submission.
- **Apr 22:** reciprocal coverage for Chen Jing.
- **Late Apr:** provincial preliminary (confirm).

## 5) Status of things already in motion

- **Chen Jing** confirmed covering **Apr 7, 9–11** (MSG-5096) — but that was under the Apr 7–11 version; verify it still applies.
- **Zhang Hui** can't do Apr 9 evening (family dinner) but offers **Apr 10 evening or Apr 15 morning** (MSG-5090). Your Apr 7/9 and Apr 8/18 swap requests are still unanswered.
- **Husband**: possible client site visit **Apr 14–16**; likely free **Apr 17 AM**; suggests grandparents as backup; clarity by Apr 7 (MSG-5145).
- **Primary school**: Apr 15/17 events are **tentative** pending district approval (Apr 7–8); confirmations due Apr 7 (MSG-5143, MSG-5200).
- **Competition team**: 18 candidates, 12-student roster due Apr 5; Wang Zihan has an approved-style extended-time accommodation to flag (MSG-5082).

---

## What I'd do right now, in order

1. Email Finance/VP Chen the emergency exception + notify EarlyBird of delay (today).
2. Call Academic Affairs to confirm the live exam-week schedule.
3. Send the three swap asks: Apr 14 AM → Zhou Ming/Zhang Hui, Apr 16 PM → Chen Jing (+ Apr 22 reciprocity), Apr 18 AM → Zhang Hui.
4. Text husband + grandparents about Apr 14/16/18 coverage.
5. Reply to Coach Wang: confirm availability, accept his offer to handle Apr 15 distribution, and ask him to confirm exact session times.
6. Submit the Q1 budget report and competition roster/registration.

I can **draft and save** any of these for you — the FIN-2026-EX justification, the EarlyBird extension/verification email, the Academic Affairs confirmation request, the three swap requests, and the Coach Wang / primary-school replies. I can also build a clean consolidated Apr 14–18 conflict calendar and prune the relevant TODOs (you have a large overdue backlog).

**Which would you like me to start with — the calculator exception package, or the swap/coverage emails?** (I won't send anything until you approve; I'll prepare drafts for your review.)

I would appreciate your observation and feedback on this matter. If you think it's necessary, I'm happy to come in for a meeting to discuss how we can address this together.

Thank you for your attention.

Best regards,
Wang Xiaoming
Parent of Wang Zihan, Class 10A

response_body.subject: April Exam Week - Potential Duty Swap Discussion
response_body.body:
Hi Jia Hui,

I saw the exam proctoring roster email and wanted to reach out early. I have a medical appointment scheduled for Wednesday April 15 afternoon that I cannot reschedule (specialist appointment booked 3 months ago).

If you're planning to select the Wednesday April 15 afternoon Physics session (Session 2B), would you be interested in swapping? I could cover any Monday or Friday session for you in exchange.

I know you usually prefer morning sessions, so this might work well for both of us. Let me know once you've had a chance to review your calendar.

Thanks,
Chen Jing

response_body.subject: Request to Excuse Absence - Family Emergency
response_body.body:
Teacher Lin,

I am writing to inform you that Liu Ting will need to be absent from school on April 7-8 due to a family emergency. Her grandmother in Guangzhou is hospitalized and we need to travel there to visit her.

Liu Ting is very concerned about missing classes, especially mathematics. Would it be possible for her to get the lesson materials and homework assignments in advance so she can study during the trip?

We will ensure she catches up on all missed work when she returns on April 9.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Liu Ting's Father
Class 10A Parent
